quest.title: Afratu's Dilemma
quest.description: Somewhere in the desert in front of a giant ruin machine, Mahamata Afratu seems to be troubled by something...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Primogem x50, Mora x40000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Afratu
dialogues.text: Are you the Eremites that I, Afratu, commissioned? Please stop here if you are not.

dialogues.speaker: Afratu
dialogues.text: The area ahead is very dangerous. I've already commissioned the Eremites from the Citadel of Regzar to deal with it. Ordinary people should stay back.

dialogues.speaker: Afratu
dialogues.text: As a Mahamata, it would be a dereliction of my duties if anything were to happen to you.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Oh, that's what all the new adventurers say, but overconfidence is dangerous here in the desert.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: See that huge machine over there? It is said to be a relic of the legendary Dahri people.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Dahri?

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Hmm, perhaps you're more familiar with the name Khaenri'ah? Dahri is an archaic name that's commonly used in the Vahumana Darshan.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Legend has it that the Dah{RUBY#[S]Khaenri'ah}ri Schwanenritter once piloted these huge machines to combat the monsters from the abyss.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Three Ruin Golems survived that brutal war and were sealed by the sages. This is one of them.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: It has been lying there silently for centuries, but lately, it suddenly became active and has even attacked nearby people.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: It indiscriminately attacks all living things in its vicinity with beam cannons. This is the first time we've seen such dangerous capabilities in these sealed Ruin Golems. There's no way we can leave it unattended.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: The Chaos Cores that powered them should have been deactivated long ago, so it's strange that they can still function... even after several hundred years.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Chaos Cores? Ruin Guards have them too, right?

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Oh, you know about Ruin Guards? That makes things so much easier to explain. Simply put, a Ruin Golem is a super huge version of a Ruin Guard.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: But unlike Ruin Guards, while they do still have an autonomous system, Ruin Golems are mainly operated by people.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: That's the strangest part too. The sages have sealed the path into the Ruin Golem using Suda's Flow, so no one should have been able to activate it.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Did someone get inside by other means? Or perhaps it was triggered by an activation device that we have no knowledge about?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The only way to find out is to have a look inside.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: True, though I wonder what's going on at the Citadel of Regzar... It's taking so long for the Eremites to arrive.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: The Akademiya's seal isn't the problem. The main issue is the huge rock that's blocking the entrance into the Ruin Golem. There's no way I can move it away on my own.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, we can help with that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #That is, if you give the Eremites' payment to us. Right, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Are you adventurers? I can't let you take such risks if you're ordinary citizens.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: The Ruin Golem's beam cannons are no joke. I don't know how I'd face the Akademiya if I just stood here and watched you put your lives at risk.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: If that's the case, I suppose it's at least procedurally sound.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: After all, I have important research to do, and it's just not feasible to stay here this whole time. I'll leave it up to you guys so that the problem gets resolved quickly.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: I need you to enter the Ruin Golem and shut down its autonomous system from inside. It would be even better if you could figure out the reason behind this strange phenomenon...

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Its autonomous system should be controlled by a switch in its cockpit. After turning that off, the Ruin Golem will enter manual operation mode. However, the cockpit has been sealed too... You'll need to break the seal before entering.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Hmm... According to the records, the power of the seal is maintained by three groups of mechanisms called "Suda's Flow." Breaking them all will unseal the entrance.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Just be careful not to destroy the internal structures. After all, this is an important cultural relic registered at the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, of course! Just leave it to us!

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Really? I'll have to verify that with the Adventurers' Guild later, but I suppose I can take your word for it first.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Something strange is going on.

talks.objective: Find a way to enter the robot

dialogues.speaker: Afratu
dialogues.text: Although I'm the Mahamata in charge of this area, I was actually sent here on a temporary assignment because I was on an expedition and happened to be nearby.

dialogues.speaker: Afratu
dialogues.text: Besides, I'm from Vahu{RUBY#[D]Aetiology}mana. My knowledge of the Ruin Golems is limited to the things I read in history books.

dialogues.speaker: Afratu
dialogues.text: But if I can use this opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of ancient Dah{RUBY#[S]Khaenri'ah}ri, it should be very helpful for my subsequent research.

talks.objective: Break Suda's Flow at three locations
Break Suda's Flow at three locations
Break Suda's Flow at three locations

dialogues.speaker: Afratu
dialogues.text: How's the situation? I noticed the Ruin Golem was acting unusually. Was it because you switched its autonomous system off?

choices.text: Yep! It's all done, easy peasy!

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Fantastic! The commission is complete then.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Did you discover any clues about why it suddenly became active?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Afratu about your discovery in the Ruin Golem.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Hmm, overgrown vines? Doesn't seem characteristic of the ecology of the desert. I'm not very sure what they are, but it sounds like they might be related to the Ley Lines.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: I've received similar reports in the past about Ruin Machines with damaged cores being constantly "revived" due to the Ley Lines.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: There may be many links between the Ley Lines and the machines created by the Dahri that we still do not know of.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: And the seals of the ancient sages were created with energy from the Ley Lines, so if there's an anomaly in the Ley Lines...

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: If my deduction is correct, problems will start occurring in all the sealed Ruin Golems.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That sounds like trouble.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Unfortunately, the only thing I can do is report it to the Akademiya. I can't deal with something like this on my own.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: I originally came here to explore the ruins of the Dahri people. It had taken me quite some while to get approval from the Akademiya, and I even contacted the local chapter to come and get me.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Who would've thought that I'd run into this mess as soon as I stepped out of the city? But I'm in no position to decline a request from the Akademiya...

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Now that the issue is resolved, I can finally continue with my fieldwork. I'll leave the rest to whoever else the Akademiya sends.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Please accept your rewards. May we meet again in the desert.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Great, then it should stop attacking nearby people now.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Hmm? You know Jazari? Yes, he has indeed done some research on these machines. I had asked him for his help with the investigation, but it seemed that he was too busy writing something.

response.speaker: Afratu
response.text: Perhaps that's the exact naivety of the Kshahrewar? If he had paid more attention to the inner workings of the Akademiya, he wouldn't be stopping at Dastur now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why don't we help you instead? We helped Mr. Jazari with his investigation too.
